reason: The Spanish 'laminar(es) margen(es) escama(s)' can mean scales on the margin of a leaf lamina or the margin of a scale's own lamina. The values (glabrous, shape) don't settle which. 'Scale' is already a trichome synonym (PO_0000282), but the organ that carries it is unclear.

label: underleaf
definition: A non-vascular leaf (PO:0025075) of a leafy liverwort that belongs to the ventral row of leaves on the stem. It is usually smaller than the lateral leaves and differs from them in shape.
reason: Neither PO nor FLOPO has a class for the liverwort underleaf. Leafy-liverwort floras describe it all the time (entire, toothed, plane). Once the class exists, the margin follows from the margin region rule. Propose it to PO (Bryophytes subset).
Exact: 'blade' is a synonym of leaf lamina (PO_0020039), and PO has the base class. The values (cuneate, cordate, attenuate, truncate) are leaf-base shapes.

label: thallus air pore
parent: is_a PO:0025117 plant anatomical space; part_of PO:0030027 thallus
definition: A plant anatomical space (PO:0025117) that forms an opening in the upper epidermis of a liverwort thallus (PO:0030027) over an air chamber. It is surrounded by one or more rings of epidermal cells and has no guard cells.
reason: These are the air pores of complex-thalloid liverworts. The values fit: simple or raised, a diameter, a number of rows of surrounding cells, 'without epidermal pores'. They are not stomata (PO_0008032 needs guard cells). PO has no class. Propose it upstream to PO.
Narrower: the tubular part of the hypanthium (floral cup). Floras often use 'hypanthium tube' for the hypanthium as a whole. The values are length, inflated, ribbed, funnel-shaped.

A hypopodium is the axis below the prophylls. Floras use it for the basal internode of a lateral shoot, or for the part of a pedicel or inflorescence branch below its bracteoles. The examples (2-7 cm × 0.5-1 mm, light pink, velutinous) don't say which axis is meant. If the flora's family is known, it could become shoot axis internode (PO_0005005) or pedicel (PO_0009052) in basal position.
Pattern 12, part of a qualified whole: a sepal of a female floret ('floret' is a synonym of flower, PO_0009046). 'pistillate' is already a bearer-quality context word (female, PATO_0000383).
Narrower: resin canals seen as lines in the leaf lamina. The values (visible, continuous or intermittent, branched) describe the canals as seen in the leaf.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) with star shaped (PATO_0002065); the ray count as a count of its arms
reason: These are the lateral arms of stellate hairs ('lateral rays 4-8'), and the only value is a count. PO's trichome branch is obsolete, and multicellular trichome branch cell (PO_0025163) is a cell, not an arm. Record it as a count quality of the stellate trichome. Add a 'trichome arm' class only if counts like this turn up in other floras.
Exact: the filament that carries the anther (French 'filets').

Pattern 18, position in a series: the middle awn of a three-awned lemma, as in Aristida and Stipagrostis. 'central' already maps to median, but 'awn' must be added to the organs that word applies to in config/flora_context_words.tsv.
Pattern 12: 'female' qualifies the flower, not the sepal ('sépales des fleurs ♀'). The sex quality belongs to the flower, as the note on the 'male' context word says.
Leaf plus the 'abaxial' surface context word. The values are indumentum (pilose, glabrate), which the surface pattern covers.

PO gives 'nutlet' as an exact synonym of nut fruit. The apex (mucronate, rostrate, rounded) is the apex region context word. In Lamiaceae and Boraginaceae the nutlet is morphologically a mericarp (PO_0020075). Review that if the family context is known.
Exact: PO defines coma as the tuft of seed trichomes at the micropyle. The values (length to 4 cm, ferrugineous, white) fit the seed hairs of Apocynaceae.

target: inflorescence flower pedicel (PO_0009052) of staminate flower (PO_0025600)
reason: Pattern 12: the pedicel of male flowers. The pedicel carries the flower rather than being part of it, but 'calyx of male flowers' is handled the same way.

Pattern 04, state of the bearer. It covers both readings: the blade of a sterile frond and the sterile segment (trophophore) of an Ophioglossaceae leaf. 'sterile' is already a context word, and 'lamina sterile' already exists as FLOPO_0000152.
Spanish 'vaina' can mean a leaf sheath (PO_0020104), the sheathing cataphylls on orchid pseudobulbs ('revestido de 3 vainas'), or a legume pod. Without context the bearer can't be chosen.

label: labellum callus
parent: is_a PO:0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of FLOPO_0980978 orchid labellum
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is a thickened outgrowth on the adaxial surface of an orchid labellum (FLOPO_0980978), usually near its base. It often has ridges, keels or tubercles.
reason: Bare 'callus' was rejected because it needs its organ. Here the organ is named, and the Spanish orchid examples (callo linear-oblongo, tuberculoso) fit the orchid labellum. Do not use plant callus (PO_0005052). FLOPO class only, because the labellum itself is FLOPO.
Narrower: 'pinnule' (an ultimate segment of a compound leaf or frond) is a synonym of leaflet (PO_0020049), and PO has the leaflet margin class.
Exact: 'stamen' only repeats the whole the connective belongs to.

label: closing body
parent: is_a PO:0025001 cardinal organ part; part_of PO:0030091 capsule fruit
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of the hygrochastic capsule fruit (PO:0030091) of Aizoaceae. It is a tubercle or plug at the opening of a locule that partly closes the locule when the capsule opens.
reason: A specific Aizoaceae fruit structure ('closing bodies absent', hook-shaped, white). It is a real structure, but no PO class or rule covers it. Keep it in FLOPO first; it is too family-specific to propose to PO now.

target: floral corona (FLOPO_0985020), proximal region (the connate tube)
reason: The fused basal tube of a staminal or corolline corona (Apocynaceae; cupular, membranous, toothed, 0.3-0.5 mm). It is a region of the existing corona class, so no new term is needed.

Narrower: in leaf architecture, intersecondary veins run between the secondaries, like them but shorter. They are not secondary (PO_0020140) or tertiary (PO_0008021) veins, so the general lamina vein class is the honest target.
A perianth segment of an undifferentiated perianth is a tepal (5, unequal, membranous, as in Amaranthaceae and monocots). This is near-exact; fix the hyphenated form in tokenization as well.
Exact: Spanish for perispore, which FLOPO already has. The values (loose, reticulate, crested, echinulate) are fern spore ornamentation.

Narrower: stipules fused into a sheath, as in the interpetiolar sheath of Rubiaceae or the ocrea-like sheaths of other families. The sheathing itself is the quality sheathing (FLOPO:0991105); the values are truncate, rounded, caducous.

label: leaf lobule
parent: is_a PO:0025514 phyllome lamina lobe; part_of PO:0025075 non-vascular leaf
definition: A phyllome lamina lobe (PO:0025514) that is the smaller, ventral lobe of the folded two-lobed leaf of a leafy liverwort. It is often inflated into a water sac.
reason: Bare 'lobule' was rejected because it needs its organ. Here the organ is the liverwort leaf, and the values (inflated, oblique, rectangular, 0.4-0.6 mm) fit the lobule of Lejeuneaceae and Frullaniaceae, a key character there. Propose it to PO together with underleaf.
Leaflet plus the adaxial surface context word ('haz' in Spanish). The values (dark, glossy, glabrous) fit the surface pattern.
A count fragment ('Sori one to each lobe', 'each with 3-4 spines'). It is a container phrase like the rejected 'per node' and 'per ocreate fascicle'; the lobe's organ is not named.
